newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman stocks rise 2.1 percent, market seen steadier.
newsitem.headline: Oman stocks rise 2.1 percent, market seen steadier.

text.p: Shares on the Oman stock exchange continued to advance this week with the stock market index rising 2.1 percent to 336.05 points.
A Gulf Investment Services report said the market had reached a record high but said the upward trend was slowing.
"Investors and market watchers seem enthusiastic and complaints are few," the report said, adding the market was expected to stabilise over the coming week.
Among climbers in the week to Wednesday was the National Bank of Oman, which built on the previous week's gains to close at 8.450 from 8.350 rials a week earlier.
Muscat Insurance rose to a 3.320 rial end from the previous week's 3.050 after announcing a sharp rise in first half net profit to 1.085 million rials from 394,143 rials.
Bank Muscat al-Ahli al-Omani closed at 8.220 from 7.950 rials.
National Biscuit Industries, which had climbed over one rial since early July, was steady at 6.500 rials.
Al Ahlia Portfolio Securities maintained its upward mobility and firmed to 9.450 rials from 9.320 rials a week ago. The stock has firmed over 1.5 rials since the beginning of last month.

Gulf Investment Services closed at 5.550 rials from 5.470 last week. A new share offer to raise the brokerage firm's capital to six million rials from four million will open on Saturday and subscription will end on September 1.

Oman Savings and Finance Bank gained 0.200 rials to end the week at 3.250 ahead of its merger with the Commercial Bank of Oman (CBO) on Saturday. This brings the share price level with CBO's closing price, up from 3.060 last week.
In May shareholders voted on the merger, stipulating that one CBO share be equal to one OSFB share after the merger.
Alliance Housing Bank reversed some of the previous week's losses, rising to 1.990 rials from 1.970. ($1=0.377 rial)
